subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A cheetah can run at 144 km/h. What is its speed in metres per second?
explanation: Multiply by 5/18: 144 × 5/18 = 40 m/s.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Convert a speed of 40 m/s into km/h.
explanation: Multiply by 18/5: 40 × 18/5 = 144 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A bird flies at 10 metres per second. What is its speed in kilometres per hour?
explanation: Multiply by 18/5: 10 × 18/5 = 36 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An athlete runs at 5 m/s. Express this speed in km/h.
explanation: Multiply by 18/5: 5 × 18/5 = 18 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A man walks 350 metres every minute. What is his speed in km/h?
explanation: 350 m per minute = 350 × 60 = 21000 m per hour = 21 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train 425 m long passes an electric pole in 17 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
explanation: Speed = 425/17 = 25 m/s = 25 × 18/5 = 90 km/h (a pole has no length).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A 280-metre train crosses a signal post in 8 seconds. Find its speed in km/h.
explanation: Speed = 280/8 = 35 m/s = 35 × 18/5 = 126 km/h (a pole has no length).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train of length 400 m goes past a man standing on the platform in 20 seconds. How fast is the train moving in km/h?
explanation: Speed = 400/20 = 20 m/s = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h (a pole has no length).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: How long will a train 100 m long, running at 90 km/h, take to pass a telegraph pole?
explanation: 90 km/h = 25 m/s; time = 100/25 = 4 seconds.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train 360 m long moves at 108 km/h. In how many seconds will it cross a tree beside the track?
explanation: 108 km/h = 30 m/s; time = 360/30 = 12 seconds.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A goods train of length 120 m travels at 108 km/h. How many seconds does it take to pass a signalman?
explanation: 108 km/h = 30 m/s; time = 120/30 = 4 seconds.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train running at 36 km/h crosses a pole in 14 seconds. What is the length of the train?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An express train at 36 km/h passes a lamp post in 16 seconds. How long is the train?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train 85 m long passes a man walking at 18 km/h in the same direction in 17 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
explanation: Relative speed = 85/17 = 5 m/s = 18 km/h; train speed = 18 + 18 = 36 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train running at 54 km/h passes a man walking at 18 km/h in the opposite direction in 10 seconds. What is the length of the train?
explanation: Relative speed = 54 + 18 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s; length = 20 × 10 = 200 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A cyclist rides at 18 km/h beside a railway line. A train going the same way at 90 km/h takes 9 seconds to pass him. How long is the train?
explanation: Relative speed = 90 − 18 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s; length = 20 × 9 = 180 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: How long does a 320 m train running at 54 km/h take to pass a man jogging towards it at 18 km/h?
explanation: Relative speed = 54 + 18 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s; time = 320/20 = 16 s.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A 850 m long train clears a 150 m platform in 25 seconds. Find its speed in km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train 100 m long crosses a bridge 110 m long in 14 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A goods train 160 m long takes 11 seconds to go completely through a tunnel 280 m long. How fast is it going in km/h?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: How many seconds will a 190 m train running at 36 km/h take to cross a platform 170 m long?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train 100 m long, moving at 36 km/h, has to cross a bridge of length 160 m. How long will it take?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: At 108 km/h, how long does a train of length 1,090 m take to pass completely over a 200 m viaduct?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train 190 m long running at 36 km/h crosses a platform in 42 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
explanation: 36 km/h = 10 m/s; distance in 42 s = 420 m = train + platform; so the answer is 420 − 190 = 230 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A 380 m long train at 72 km/h takes 24 seconds to cross a bridge. How long is the bridge?
explanation: 72 km/h = 20 m/s; distance in 24 s = 480 m = train + platform; so the answer is 480 − 380 = 100 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Travelling at 36 km/h, a 250-metre train passes through a tunnel in 38 seconds. Find the length of the tunnel.
explanation: 36 km/h = 10 m/s; distance in 38 s = 380 m = train + platform; so the answer is 380 − 250 = 130 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train running at 108 km/h crosses a 400 m platform in 24 seconds. How long is the train?
explanation: 108 km/h = 30 m/s; distance in 24 s = 720 m = train + bridge; so the answer is 720 − 400 = 320 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train crosses a bridge 320 m long in 38 seconds at a speed of 54 km/h. Find the length of the train.
explanation: 54 km/h = 15 m/s; distance in 38 s = 570 m = train + bridge; so the answer is 570 − 320 = 250 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train passes a pole in 11 seconds and a platform 350 m long in 25 seconds. What is the length of the train?
explanation: The extra 14 s cover the 350 m platform, so speed = 25 m/s; train length = 25 × 11 = 275 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train takes 10 seconds to pass a signal and 24 seconds to cross a bridge 350 m long. What is its speed in km/h?
explanation: The extra 14 s are spent covering the 350 m platform: speed = 350/14 = 25 m/s = 90 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train crosses a man standing on a platform in 5 seconds and the 135 m platform itself in 14 seconds. What is the length of the train?
explanation: The extra 9 s cover the 135 m platform, so speed = 15 m/s; train length = 15 × 5 = 75 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two cars start at the same time from towns 600 km apart and drive towards each other at 80 km/h and 70 km/h. After how many hours will they meet?
explanation: Moving towards each other, the gap closes at 80 + 70 = 150 km/h; time = 600/150 = 4 hours.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two buses leave two cities 340 km apart at 8 a.m. and travel towards each other at 90 km/h and 80 km/h. How many hours after 8 a.m. do they meet?
explanation: Moving towards each other, the gap closes at 90 + 80 = 170 km/h; time = 340/170 = 2 hours.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two cyclists 38 km apart ride towards each other at 16 km/h and 22 km/h. In how many hours will they meet?
explanation: Moving towards each other, the gap closes at 16 + 22 = 38 km/h; time = 38/38 = 1 hours.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two trains start from stations 360 km apart and run towards each other at 40 km/h and 80 km/h. How far from the first station will they meet?
explanation: They meet after 360/120 = 3 h; the first covers 40 × 3 = 120 km.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Tariq and Kamran set off towards each other from points 27 km apart, walking at 6 km/h and 3 km/h. How far will Tariq have walked when they meet?
explanation: They meet after 27/9 = 3 h; the first covers 6 × 3 = 18 km.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A policeman spots a thief 102 m ahead of him. The thief runs at 3 m/s and the policeman at 6 m/s. In how many seconds will the thief be caught?
explanation: The gap closes at 6 − 3 = 3 m/s; time = 102/3 = 34 s.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two runners on a straight road are 22 m apart and run in the same direction, the faster one behind, at 7 m/s and 5 m/s. How long before the faster one draws level?
explanation: The gap closes at 7 − 5 = 2 m/s; time = 22/2 = 11 s.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A car leaves a town at 50 km/h. 3 hours later a second car sets out from the same place along the same road at 80 km/h. How long after starting will the second car overtake the first?
explanation: Head start = 50 × 3 = 150 km, closed at 80 − 50 = 30 km/h: 150/30 = 5 hours after the second car starts.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two trains 320 m and 580 m long run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 90 km/h and 72 km/h. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
explanation: Relative speed = 90 + 72 = 162 km/h = 45 m/s; distance = 320 + 580 = 900 m; time = 20 s.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two trains of lengths 80 m and 70 m are moving in the same direction on parallel tracks at 72 km/h and 54 km/h. How long will the faster train take to pass the slower one completely?
explanation: Relative speed = 72 − 54 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s; distance = 80 + 70 = 150 m; time = 30 s.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two trains running in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h cross each other in 30 seconds. If one train is 170 m long, how long is the other?
explanation: Relative speed = 54 + 36 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s; together they cover 25 × 30 = 750 m, so the other train is 750 − 170 = 580 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two cars leave the same petrol station at the same time and drive in opposite directions at 50 km/h and 70 km/h. How far apart are they after 3 hours?
explanation: Opposite directions: gap grows at 120 km/h; after 3 h the distance is 360 km.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two boys start from the same point and cycle in the same direction at 14 km/h and 9 km/h. How far apart will they be after 5 hours?
explanation: Same direction: gap grows at 5 km/h; after 5 h the distance is 25 km.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A man drives to his office at 70 km/h and returns home by the same road at 30 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
explanation: For equal distances average speed = 2ab/(a + b) = 2 × 70 × 30/100 = 42 km/h (not the simple mean 50).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A cyclist goes up a hill at 15 km/h and comes down the same road at 10 km/h. Find his average speed for the round trip.
explanation: For equal distances average speed = 2ab/(a + b) = 2 × 15 × 10/25 = 12 km/h (not the simple mean 12.5).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A boat travels to an island at 30 km/h and comes back at 45 km/h. What is its average speed over the two trips?
explanation: For equal distances average speed = 2ab/(a + b) = 2 × 30 × 45/75 = 36 km/h (not the simple mean 37.5).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A car covers the first half of a journey at 60 km/h and the second half at 40 km/h. What is its average speed for the journey?
explanation: For equal distances average speed = 2ab/(a + b) = 2 × 60 × 40/100 = 48 km/h (not the simple mean 50).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A courier rides from Multan to a nearby village at 30 km/h and returns by the same route at 45 km/h. His average speed for the round trip is:
explanation: For equal distances average speed = 2ab/(a + b) = 2 × 30 × 45/75 = 36 km/h (not the simple mean 37.5).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A bus travels 240 km in 3 hours and then 200 km in 5 hours. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
explanation: Total distance = 240 + 200 = 440 km in 8 h; average speed = 55 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train runs at 70 km/h for 2 hours and then at 30 km/h for 3 hours. What is its average speed?
explanation: Total distance = 140 + 90 = 230 km in 5 h; average speed = 46 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A tractor moves along a road at 100 km/h for 2 hours and then along a motorway service lane at 40 km/h for 4 hours. What is its average speed?
explanation: Total distance = 200 + 160 = 360 km in 6 h; average speed = 60 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A man travels to a town at 20 km/h. At what speed must he return so that his average speed for the round trip is 30 km/h?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A van goes to a market at 20 km/h. How fast must it come back along the same road to average 35 km/h over the whole trip?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A person covers three equal distances at 20 km/h, 30 km/h and 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole distance?
explanation: Take each distance as D: average speed = 3/(1/20 + 1/30 + 1/60) = 30 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A motorist covers 90 km at 30 km/h and the next 210 km at 70 km/h. What is his average speed over the whole distance?
explanation: Time = 90/30 + 210/70 = 6 h for 300 km; average speed = 50 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In a 200 m race, Noreen finishes in 28 seconds and Haris in 32 seconds. By how many metres does Noreen beat Haris?
explanation: In 28 s the slower runner covers 200 × 28/32 = 175 m, so the winner leads by 200 − 175 = 25 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Hira can run 400 m in 45 s, and Hamza can run the same distance in 50 s. If they race over 400 m, by what distance does Hira win?
explanation: In 45 s the slower runner covers 400 × 45/50 = 360 m, so the winner leads by 400 − 360 = 40 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two athletes run a 400 m race. One takes 51 seconds and the other 60 seconds. When the winner crosses the line, how far behind is the other?
explanation: In 51 s the slower runner covers 400 × 51/60 = 340 m, so the winner leads by 400 − 340 = 60 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In a 1,000 m race, Zainab beats Asad by 50 m. If Zainab finishes in 171 seconds, how long does Asad take to finish?
explanation: The loser runs 950 m in 171 s, so the full 1000 m takes 171 × 1000/950 = 180 s.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Hamza beats Iqra by 10 metres in a 200 m race and finishes in 38 seconds. What is Iqra’s speed?
explanation: When the winner finishes in 38 s, the loser has run 190 m; speed = 190/38 = 5 m/s.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A runner wins a 100 m race by 5 m, crossing the line in 19 seconds. What is the loser’s time for the full distance?
explanation: The loser runs 95 m in 19 s, so the full 100 m takes 19 × 100/95 = 20 s.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Ayesha runs faster than Salman, their speeds being in the ratio 4:3. How many metres of start should Ayesha give Salman in a 200 m race so that they finish together?
explanation: While the faster runs 200 m, the slower runs 200 × 3/4 = 150 m; start needed = 50 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The speeds of two swimmers are in the ratio 5:4. In a 1,000 m race, how much of a head start must the faster give the slower for a dead heat?
explanation: While the faster runs 1000 m, the slower runs 1000 × 4/5 = 800 m; start needed = 200 m.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In a 1,000 m race, Naveed beats Farah by 40 m or 9 seconds. How long does Naveed take to run the race?
explanation: The loser runs 40 m in 9 s, so he takes 1000 × 9/40 = 225 s for the race; the winner takes 225 − 9 = 216 s.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A runner beats another by 25 metres or 4 seconds in a 1,000 m race. What is the winner’s time?
explanation: The loser runs 25 m in 4 s, so he takes 1000 × 4/25 = 160 s for the race; the winner takes 160 − 4 = 156 s.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In a 1,000 m race, Areeba beats Hira by 25 m, and Hira beats Hamza by 20 m. By how many metres does Areeba beat Hamza?
explanation: When P finishes, Q has run 975 m; R runs 980/1000 of that = 955.5 m, so P beats R by 44.5 m (slightly less than 25 + 20).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Over 200 m, P beats Q by 10 m and Q beats R by 20 m. By what distance would P beat R over the same course?
explanation: When P finishes, Q has run 190 m; R runs 180/200 of that = 171 m, so P beats R by 29 m (slightly less than 10 + 20).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Walking at 4 km/h, a student reaches school 5 minutes late. At 6 km/h he reaches 15 minutes early. How far is the school from his home?
explanation: The two times differ by 20 min = 0.333333333 h: D/4 − D/6 = 0.333333333 ⇒ D = 4 km.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: If a man cycles at 15 km/h he is 20 minutes late for work, but at 20 km/h he is 12 minutes early. What distance does he cycle to work?
explanation: The two times differ by 32 min = 0.533333333 h: D/15 − D/20 = 0.533333333 ⇒ D = 32 km.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A bus running at 50 km/h arrives 5 minutes late; at 75 km/h it would arrive 6 minutes early. What is the length of the route?
explanation: The two times differ by 11 min = 0.183333333 h: D/50 − D/75 = 0.183333333 ⇒ D = 27.5 km.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Driving at 45 km/h, Bilal misses a train by 20 minutes. Had he driven at 70 km/h, he would have reached the station 10 minutes before the train left. How far is the station?
explanation: The two times differ by 30 min = 0.5 h: D/45 − D/70 = 0.5 ⇒ D = 63 km.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A clerk walking at 9 km/h reaches his office 5 minutes late. If he walks at 10 km/h he arrives exactly on time. How far is his office?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A van travelling at 60 km/h reaches a village 10 minutes late. At 85 km/h it would have been on time. What is the distance to the village?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Walking at 3/4 of his usual speed, a man is 31 minutes late. What is his usual time for the journey?
explanation: At 3/4 of the speed the time is 4/3 of usual, i.e. 1/3 of the usual time extra = 31 min, so the usual time = 31 × 3/1 = 93 min.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A train running at 6/7 of its normal speed reaches its destination 12 minutes late. How long does the journey normally take?
explanation: At 6/7 of the speed the time is 7/6 of usual, i.e. 1/6 of the usual time extra = 12 min, so the usual time = 12 × 6/1 = 72 min.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: By cycling at 6/7 of her usual speed, a girl reaches college 15 minutes late. How long does she usually take?
explanation: At 6/7 of the speed the time is 7/6 of usual, i.e. 1/6 of the usual time extra = 15 min, so the usual time = 15 × 6/1 = 90 min.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A car moving at 3/5 of its usual speed takes 24 minutes longer than usual to cover a certain distance. What is its usual time for that distance?
explanation: At 3/5 of the speed the time is 5/3 of usual, i.e. 2/3 of the usual time extra = 24 min, so the usual time = 24 × 3/2 = 36 min.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The downstream speed of a boat is 15 km/h and its upstream speed is 9 km/h. What is its speed in still water?
explanation: Still-water speed = (downstream + upstream)/2 = (15 + 9)/2 = 12 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A launch travels at 11 km/h downstream and 1 km/h upstream. What is the speed of the river’s current?
explanation: Stream speed = (downstream − upstream)/2 = (11 − 1)/2 = 5 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A swimmer moves at 18 km/h with the current and 16 km/h against it. How fast would the swimmer move in still water?
explanation: Still-water speed = (downstream + upstream)/2 = (18 + 16)/2 = 17 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A boat’s speed in still water is 14 km/h and the river flows at 5 km/h. What is the boat’s speed when it goes upstream?
explanation: Against the current the speeds subtract: 14 − 5 = 9 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A boat goes 36 km downstream in 3 hours and 4 km upstream in 2 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
explanation: Downstream = 36/3 = 12 km/h, upstream = 4/2 = 2 km/h; still water = (12 + 2)/2 = 7 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A man rows 24 km with the current in 2 hours and 40 km against it in 4 hours. Find the speed of the current.
explanation: Downstream = 24/2 = 12 km/h, upstream = 40/4 = 10 km/h; stream = (12 − 10)/2 = 1 km/h.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A boat whose speed in still water is 11 km/h goes 36 km downstream in a river flowing at 1 km/h. How long does it take?
explanation: Downstream speed = 11 + 1 = 12 km/h; time = 36/12 = 3 hours.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A motorboat travels at 12 km/h in still water. How long will it take to go 32 km upstream against a current of 4 km/h?
explanation: Upstream speed = 12 − 4 = 8 km/h; time = 32/8 = 4 hours.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A boat with a speed of 6 km/h in still water goes 10 km downstream and comes back. If the river flows at 4 km/h, how long does the round trip take?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A fisherman rows 42 km up a river and back again. He rows at 10 km/h in still water and the river flows at 4 km/h. What is the total time taken?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A boat moving at 12 km/h in still water takes 3 hours to go to a place and come back. If the current flows at 4 km/h, how far away is the place?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A man rows at 3 km/h in still water. It takes him twice as long to row upstream as to row the same distance downstream. What is the speed of the stream?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: It takes a boat three times as long to go up a stretch of river as to come down it. If the boat’s still-water speed is 12 km/h, find the speed of the current.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A machine prints 85 pages per minute. How long will it take to print 3,825 pages?
explanation: Time = 3,825/85 = 45 minutes.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A typist types 50 words a minute. How long does she need to type a 3,000-word report?
explanation: Time = 3,000/50 = 60 minutes.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A pump lifts 180 litres of water per minute. How long will it take to lift 3,780 litres?
explanation: Time = 3,780/180 = 21 minutes.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A bottling plant fills 2,900 bottles an hour. How many bottles does it fill in 8 hours?
explanation: 2900 per hour × 8 hours = 23,200.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Water drips from a leaking tap at 20 ml per minute. How much water is wasted in 2 hours?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: One machine packs 60 boxes an hour and another packs 50. Working together, how long will they take to pack 220 boxes?
explanation: Combined rate = 60 + 50 = 110 per hour; time = 220/110 = 2 hours.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Two clerks can check 20 and 30 forms an hour respectively. How many hours will they take together to check 300 forms?
explanation: Combined rate = 20 + 30 = 50 per hour; time = 300/50 = 6 hours.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A car runs 18 km on a litre of petrol, and petrol costs Rs 300 a litre. What is the fuel cost of a 252 km trip?
explanation: Petrol needed = 252/18 = 14 litres; cost = 14 × 300 = Rs 4,200.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A motorcycle gives 19 km per litre of petrol. How many litres does it need for a 722 km journey?
